builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: WASP-Mem: Let Agent Organize Procedural Memory. Human Spend Effort on Diagnosis
summary: WASP-Mem replaces static, hand-built agent harnesses and prescriptive memory schemas with wiki pages that the agent itself distills from execution traces and feedback, consolidating reusable actions and recovery strategies without any model training. The cost is ongoing trace ingestion and synthesis via LLM calls (third-party APIs are sufficient), plus the key operational investment: human diagnosis of failed traces, which the paper shows is what drives sustained gains. It can fail when no human diagnosis capacity exists (self-judgment refinement is markedly weaker), when the target procedures lack repeated trace volume to consolidate, and because results are validated on a single benchmark and may not transfer to proprietary enterprise workflows.
rationale: The method is training-free, API-compatible, and storage-efficient, making it feasible on constrained infrastructure, but its central benefit depends on a human-diagnosis workflow and benchmark gains of 4.6-6.1 points that the reader must validate on their own procedures before production adoption.
technique: Agent-synthesized wiki procedural memory from execution traces

claims.statement: WASP-Mem replaces static, hand-built agent harnesses and prescriptive memory schemas with wiki pages that the agent itself distills from execution traces and feedback, consolidating reusable actions and recovery strategies without any model training. The cost is ongoing trace ingestion and synthesis via LLM calls (third-party APIs are sufficient), plus the key operational investment: human diagnosis of failed traces, which the paper shows is what drives sustained gains. It can fail when no human diagnosis capacity exists (self-judgment refinement is markedly weaker), when the target procedures lack repeated trace volume to consolidate, and because results are validated on a single benchmark and may not transfer to proprietary enterprise workflows.

On TheAgentCompany, raises checkpoint pass rate by 4.6-6.1 percentage points over the strongest baseline across three models with 57-61% less storage; one round of human diagnosis outperforms four rounds of self-judgment by 7.0-10.9 percentage points.
